tools.description: Terminate a session's entire process group and remove the session from the host (docs/CLI.md §6.7).
tools.name: close_session

final_sequence.description: Cumulative output byte offset at removal.

session_ref.description: Opaque session handle that was closed.

tools.description: Close a previously opened tunnel by its tunnel_id (docs/CLI.md §6.9).
tools.name: close_tunnel

closed.description:
`true` if a tunnel was closed; `false` if none existed with that id
(idempotent, same pattern as `TrustRemoveData::removed`).

tunnel_id.description: Opaque tunnel handle that was asked to be closed.

tools.description: Run a single non-interactive command on a host and return its captured stdout/stderr and exit status once it completes (docs/CLI.md §6.8).

argv.description:
Program and arguments, passed to the remote verbatim (no shell
re-interpretation).

env.description: Extra environment variables layered over the remote environment.

host.description:
Host name. Until the hosts.toml directory lands (M7) this is resolved
through the trust store's pinned peers (name → address).

timeout_ms.description:
Whole-operation timeout in milliseconds (`docs/CLI.md` §9). `None`
means no timeout.

tools.name: exec

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of the remote execution in milliseconds.

remote_exit_code.description:
The remote process's real exit code (`0..=255`). This is the source
of truth; the process exit code of `qsh exec` clamps 255 → 254
(`docs/CLI.md` §4). When the process was killed by a signal this is
`128 + signo` and [`signal`](Self::signal) names it.

tools.description: Look up a single host by its local alias (docs/CLI.md §6.1).
tools.name: get_host

address.description:
`host:port` this client dials (forward hosts) or last observed from
(reverse hosts).

device_id.description:
The peer's SPKI SHA-256 fingerprint, `sha256:BASE64`
(`docs/design/architecture.md` §5) — the value pinned in the trust
store for a forward host, or the value the daemon TLS-verified for a
reverse host. Never `Hello.device_name` or any other wire display
name (`docs/design/protocol.md` §3: identity is never taken from
wire data), e.g. `"sha256:BASE64FINGERPRINT"`.

state.description:
Reachability, open string set (`docs/CLI.md` §10): `"reachable"` |
`"stale"` | `"unknown"`. A forward host is never probed for
reachability in M3, so it always reports `"unknown"` — an
unconfirmed host is never reported as `"reachable"`. A live reverse
registration (the controller is actively holding an authenticated
connection to it) is `"reachable"`; a registration whose connection
died is `"stale"` for the controller's retention window
(`docs/design/protocol.md` §11-4) before it is dropped.

tools.description: Look up a single session by its session_ref (docs/CLI.md §6.2).

session_ref.description: Opaque session handle as returned by `session.open`/`session.list`.

tools.name: get_session

created_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of session creation.

host.description: Host alias this session lives on.

last_sequence.description:
Cumulative output byte offset produced by this session so far
(`docs/CLI.md` §2.3); pass straight to `session read --after`.

session_id.description: Opaque, URL-safe session identifier issued by the host (ULID).

session_ref.description:
Opaque handle (`<host-alias>/<session_id>`, assembled by `Ops`);
callers must not construct or parse this themselves.

state.description:
Session lifecycle state — open string set: `"running"`, `"exited"`,
... (`docs/CLI.md` §10).

writer.description:
Principal string of the current writer-lease holder
(`device:…`/`user:…`/`fp:…`), or `null` when no connection holds the
lease.

tools.description: List configured forward hosts and any currently registered reverse hosts, without dialing or checking reachability for any of them (docs/CLI.md §6.1).
tools.name: list_hosts

Host.description:
A host entry as returned by `qsh hosts` / `qsh host get`
(`docs/CLI.md` §5, "Host").

Placeholder no longer describes this type: M3 Step 1 is the first thing
to fix its value vocabulary (below), even though no op emits it and no
fixture exists for it *yet* (both land in Step 5) — so this is the
*first definition* of these fields' meaning, not a documented-meaning
change that would require `/v2` (`docs/CLI.md` §10). Actual production
(`host.list`/`host.get`) lands with the M3 reverse registry and `qsh
listen`/`qsh reverse` steps later in this milestone; the host *directory*
(`hosts.toml`) is M7.

address.description:
`host:port` this client dials (forward hosts) or last observed from
(reverse hosts).

device_id.description:
The peer's SPKI SHA-256 fingerprint, `sha256:BASE64`
(`docs/design/architecture.md` §5) — the value pinned in the trust
store for a forward host, or the value the daemon TLS-verified for a
reverse host. Never `Hello.device_name` or any other wire display
name (`docs/design/protocol.md` §3: identity is never taken from
wire data), e.g. `"sha256:BASE64FINGERPRINT"`.

state.description:
Reachability, open string set (`docs/CLI.md` §10): `"reachable"` |
`"stale"` | `"unknown"`. A forward host is never probed for
reachability in M3, so it always reports `"unknown"` — an
unconfirmed host is never reported as `"reachable"`. A live reverse
registration (the controller is actively holding an authenticated
connection to it) is `"reachable"`; a registration whose connection
died is `"stale"` for the controller's retention window
(`docs/design/protocol.md` §11-4) before it is dropped.

hosts.description: Every host visible to this caller, forward and reverse together.

tools.description: List sessions on one host, or best-effort fan out across every pinned host when no host is given (docs/CLI.md §6.2).

host.description: Host alias to list; `None` = every configured host.

tools.name: list_sessions

Session.description:
A session entry as returned by `qsh sessions` / `qsh session get`
(`docs/CLI.md` §5, "Session").

This is the JSON DTO: the wire `SessionInfo` carries
`session_id/state/writer/created_at/last_sequence` only, and the client
`Ops` layer adds `session_ref`/`host` from its local alias knowledge
(ADR-0007).

created_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of session creation.

host.description: Host alias this session lives on.

last_sequence.description:
Cumulative output byte offset produced by this session so far
(`docs/CLI.md` §2.3); pass straight to `session read --after`.

session_id.description: Opaque, URL-safe session identifier issued by the host (ULID).

session_ref.description:
Opaque handle (`<host-alias>/<session_id>`, assembled by `Ops`);
callers must not construct or parse this themselves.

state.description:
Session lifecycle state — open string set: `"running"`, `"exited"`,
... (`docs/CLI.md` §10).

writer.description:
Principal string of the current writer-lease holder
(`device:…`/`user:…`/`fp:…`), or `null` when no connection holds the
lease.

UnreachableHost.description:
One host `session.list` could not reach — its alias plus the error it
would have produced on its own (`docs/CLI.md` §6.2).

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Automation must not parse this.

sessions.description: Sessions visible under the caller's `session.list` ACL scope.

unreachable.description:
Hosts that could not be asked when `qsh sessions` fans out over
every pinned host (`docs/CLI.md` §6.2). Absent/empty when every host
answered, and always empty for a single-host request (that is a
plain error). Additive (`qsh.cli/v1`).

tools.description: Open a new interactive PTY session on a host, running a login shell or a given argv (docs/CLI.md §6.3).

argv.description:
Program and arguments (`--` argv), passed verbatim — no shell
re-interpretation. Empty = the remote account's login shell.

env.description:
Extra environment variables layered over the remote login-shell
environment.

term.description: `TERM` to export in the session; `None` = remote default.

user.description:
The `user` half of `qsh user@host` — a hint checked against the
remote serve account's login name (`docs/CLI.md` §7); never an
identity (the principal always comes from the certificate).

tools.name: open_session

initial_sequence.description: Cumulative output offset at creation — `0` for a fresh session.

session_ref.description: Opaque session handle for every later `session.*` call.

tools.description: Open a local or remote TCP port forward through a host (docs/CLI.md §6.9).

bind.description: The `[bind:]` prefix, when present; `None` = caller-side default.

forward_host.description:
The `host` component of the forward spec (the dial target host —
distinct from this request's own `host` field, which is the QSH
peer).

forward_port.description: The `host_port` component of the forward spec.

tools.name: open_tunnel

actual_port.description:
The port actually bound — the kernel-assigned one for a `0`
request, and the requested one when it was granted as asked
(`docs/CLI.md` §6.9's `Tunnel` example carries it for a fixed-port
forward). Optional because a tunnel that is not bound yet has no
port to report; a producer that knows the bound port always fills
it, so a reader never has to fall back to splitting `bind`.

bind.description: The `[bind:]listen_port` half of the forward spec, as bound.

forward_to.description:
The `host:host_port` half of the forward spec — the dial target, in
the canonical form [`crate::wire::format_host_port`] produces (an
IPv6 literal is bracketed: `"[::1]:5432"`).

host.description:
Host alias this tunnel is on (`Ops`-filled; never present on the
wire — ADR-0007, same rule as `Session.host`).

mode.description:
Open string set: `"local"` (`-L`) or `"remote"` (`-R`) — same
open-string discipline as `Host.connection_mode` (`docs/CLI.md`
§10).

tools.description: Pull a session's buffered output and lifecycle events since a given byte offset, optionally waiting for new data to arrive (docs/CLI.md §6.4).

after_sequence.description:
Cumulative output byte offset already received (`--after`); the
reply starts right after it.

ctl_after.description:
Control-entry cursor (`--ctl-after`): the `next_ctl_after` of the
previous reply, `0` (the default) for a fresh read. Control events
(`session.exit`/`writer_changed`/`closed`) carry the offset they were
appended at and do **not** advance it, so `after_sequence` alone
cannot express "I already have the control event positioned at N";
a poller that does not echo this back sees such an event again on
every pull (`docs/CLI.md` §6.4). Additive (`qsh.cli/v1`), so it is
omitted entirely when unset.

limit_bytes.description:
Maximum output payload bytes in one reply (`--limit-bytes`); `None`
= server default.

wait_ms.description:
Long-poll wait for new output in milliseconds (`--wait`); `None` =
return immediately.

tools.name: read_session

sequence.description: Byte-offset sequence of the *end* of this chunk.

session_ref.description: Opaque session handle this event belongs to.

anyOf.description:
The requested replay range is no longer available; the reader must
resync from `available_from`.

available_from.description: Earliest sequence still available in the replay ring.

requested_after.description: The `--after` sequence the reader asked for.

session_ref.description: Opaque session handle this event belongs to.

exit_code.description: Process exit code, or `null` if terminated by signal.

sequence.description: Byte-offset sequence at the moment of exit.

session_ref.description: Opaque session handle this event belongs to.

signal.description: Signal name that terminated the process, if any.

anyOf.description:
The writer lease changed hands (stolen by another attach, or
auto-released because the owning connection died — then
`writer: null`). Broadcast to every read consumer of the session.

sequence.description: Cumulative output byte offset at the moment of the change.

session_ref.description: Opaque session handle this event belongs to.

writer.description:
Principal string of the new lease holder (same format as
`Session.writer`), or `null` when nobody holds it.

anyOf.description:
The session was removed from the broker; always the last event for
a `session_ref`.

reason.description:
Who removed the session — `"closed"` (explicit `session.close` or
serve drain), `"exit"` (child exited, TTL reaper cleaned up) or
`"ttl_expired"` (running session reaped without attach). Open
set: unknown values mean only "the session is gone".

sequence.description: Cumulative output byte offset at removal.

session_ref.description: Opaque session handle this event belongs to.

SessionEvent.description:
One `qsh.event/v1` event, tagged on `type` to match the wire examples in
`docs/CLI.md` §6.4.

Open string fields (`Closed::reason`) are modelled as `String`, not as
enums, because their value sets may grow additively (`docs/CLI.md` §10).

events.description:
`qsh.event/v1` events (`session.output`/`gap`/`exit`/
`writer_changed`/`closed`); may be empty when `wait_ms` elapsed.

next_after.description:
Cursor to resume from: pass back as `after_sequence`. Equal to the
request's `after_sequence` plus the output bytes delivered (or the
replay buffer's `available_from` after a gap). Additive
(`qsh.cli/v1`).

next_ctl_after.description:
Control-entry half of the resume cursor: pass back as `ctl_after`.
Additive (`qsh.cli/v1`).

session_ref.description: Opaque session handle the events belong to.

tools.description: Resize a session's PTY to the given terminal column/row dimensions (docs/CLI.md §6.6).
tools.name: resize_session

tools.description: Write bytes to a session's PTY input (docs/CLI.md §6.5).

data_b64.description:
Bytes to inject as terminal input, standard Base64 (`--data-b64`, or
raw stdin encoded by the CLI for `--stdin`).

tools.name: write_session

bytes_written.description: Number of input bytes accepted by the host.
